rationale: Policy: resume. Steps 1-6 only build a small deterministic workspace and every step is idempotent, so the half-finished state left by a step-7 crash (result.partial) is harmless and the same disk is still valid. Step-7 failures are overwhelmingly transient (guest-agent timeout, OOM-kill of the test runner), so retrying only step 7 on the same guest costs one command, whereas rollback needs a checkpoint tar and fresh pays a new boot plus a replay of six steps and any LLM tokens. If the guest is unreachable the policy restarts it (stop/start persistence keeps the disk). Attempts are capped at three per step, after which the run is marked failed and the guest is deleted anyway. Rollback and fresh are implemented and selectable via run_job(policy=...) for non-idempotent workloads.
